content: The second edition of the Catalogue of Mutations in Mycobacterium tuberculosis Complex and Their Association with Drug Resistance was developed by the World Health Organization (WHO) in 2023. This document provides a comprehensive reference for interpreting genetic mutations in Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTBC) and their association with resistance to various tuberculosis (TB) drugs. It builds upon the first edition published in 2021, incorporating new data and expanding the scope of analysis to include additional drugs and mutations. The catalogue is based on a systematic analysis of a large WHO database containing whole-genome sequencing (WGS) and phenotypic drug susceptibility testing (pDST) data from clinical isolates of MTBC collected globally. The second edition includes data from approximately 52,000 isolates, an increase from the 38,000 isolates analyzed in the first edition. These isolates were contributed by 67 countries, with significant representation from India and the United Kingdom. The primary goal of this updated catalogue is to improve the detection of mutations associated with resistance to both first-line and second-line TB drugs. It includes mutations linked to resistance against rifampicin (RIF), isoniazid (INH), ethambutol (EMB), pyrazinamide (PZA), and newer or repurposed drugs such as bedaquiline (BDQ), linezolid (LZD), delamanid (DLM), and pretomanid (PMD). The catalogue also provides guidance for interpreting mutations associated with resistance to drugs no longer recommended for TB treatment, such as kanamycin (KAN) and capreomycin (CAP), for historical and contextual purposes. The molecular basis of drug resistance in MTBC is well-documented for many drugs. For example, resistance to RIF is primarily caused by mutations in the rifampicin resistance-determining region (RRDR) of the rpoB gene. Similarly, resistance to INH is often linked to mutations in the katG gene or the fabG1-inhA promoter region. The catalogue categorizes mutations into five groups based on the strength and quality of evidence supporting their association with phenotypic resistance. This classification helps standardize the interpretation of genetic data and supports the development of molecular diagnostic tools. The second edition introduces several improvements over the first edition. It includes new mutations associated with resistance to BDQ and LZD, identified through laboratory-based selection experiments. Additionally, it provides early guidance for interpreting mutations linked to PMD resistance, despite the absence of a WHO-endorsed critical concentration for this drug. The catalogue also incorporates data from geographically diverse sources, addressing gaps in representation from certain regions. WHO recommends routine testing of all TB patients for resistance to RIF and INH, with additional testing for fluoroquinolones (FQs) and other second-line drugs in cases of multidrug-resistant TB (MDR-TB). The catalogue supports these efforts by serving as a standardized reference for interpreting mutations detected through next-generation sequencing (NGS) or other genotypic drug susceptibility testing (gDST) methods. The development of the second edition was led by a team of experts, including Nazir Ahmed Ismail, Carl-Michael Nathanson, and Alexei Korobitsyn, with support from global collaborators. The work was funded by grants from Unitaid and the U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID). All contributors disclosed potential conflicts of interest, and no significant conflicts were identified. This updated catalogue aims to inform the development of new and improved molecular assays for comprehensive detection of TB drug resistance. It also highlights areas for future research, such as the molecular basis of resistance to newer drugs and the development of rapid diagnostic tools for detecting resistance to these agents.
